summary: Ustaz Azlan describes the ten earliest people to accept Islam and how the call began in private. Khadijah RA was the first, followed by Ali (about 10 years old), Zayd ibn Harithah, and Abu Bakr, who then brought Uthman, Az-Zubayr, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Talhah and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. He also touches on the two-rak'ah prayer Jibril taught, the family support for the call, the house of Al-Arqam as headquarters, and the lesson that great change often begins with a small group holding to the truth.
keyPoints: Khadijah RA was the first to accept Islam and the first the Prophet SAW taught to pray.
The earliest prayer was two rak'ahs before sunrise and after sunset, according to Aisha's hadith.
Ali ibn Abi Talib, about 10 at the time, accepted Islam after taking one night to think.
Abu Bakr accepted without hesitation and brought most of the ten companions promised Paradise.
The house of Al-Arqam, from Abu Jahl's clan, became the base of the secret call for about three years.
Great change begins with a small group that holds to the truth, and being few is not the measure of right or wrong.

lessons.title: Family support starts the call
lessons.body: Khadijah's unconditional belief was Allah's gift so the call could begin.

lessons.title: Children learn prayer by seeing their parents
lessons.body: Ali asked because he saw the Prophet SAW pray; many children today never see their parents pray.

lessons.title: It is never too late to start praying
lessons.body: Anyone who has not prayed can start today.

lessons.title: Give people time to think
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW let Ali take a night to think before accepting Islam.

lessons.title: Interpersonal skills and networks help da'wah
lessons.body: Abu Bakr used his genealogy knowledge and business integrity to approach quality people.

lessons.title: Build a base first
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW planned tactically, building a base before declaring openly.

lessons.title: Change begins with small groups
lessons.body: A small group holding to the truth drives change.

lessons.title: Numbers are not the measure of truth
lessons.body: Many or few is no sign; the sign is the truth being carried.
